s: the family-run currywurst stand that's served the same corner since 1930
w: A tiny stand wedged under the elevated U2 tracks at Eberswalder Strasse, run by the same family since 1930 -- through Nazi closure of its Jewish co-owner, East German rationing, and reunification. The curry-spiced sausage is snipped and doused to order at a standing counter, watching trains rattle overhead. One of Berlin's oldest continuously run currywurst stands and a genuine Prenzlauer Berg institution.
_facts: Located at Schönhauser Allee 44a, 10435 Berlin, under the U2 viaduct at Eberswalder Strasse
Trading since 1930, run across generations of the same family
One of the oldest continuously operating currywurst stands in Berlin

s: the Mehringdamm currywurst stand with a 24-hour queue since 1980
w: Opened in 1980 by the Mehringdamm U-Bahn station, Curry 36 has grown into arguably Berlin's most famous currywurst stand -- open into the small hours and drawing a queue of night-owls, cab drivers and tourists in equal measure. The formula hasn't changed: snappy-skinned sausage, a curry-ketchup that's spawned countless imitators, and standing-room-only high tables on the pavement.
_facts: Located at Mehringdamm 36, 10961 Berlin, Kreuzberg, by the U6/U7 Mehringdamm station
Open since 1980, trading long hours into the early morning
Widely cited as Berlin's most famous currywurst stand
Known for its curry ketchup recipe as much as the sausage itself
